Construct a Structured Quadratic Penalty

Source: R/structured_penalty.R
structured_penalty.Rd

Builds the exact negative log-density of the Gaussian prior \(\beta \sim N(0, \Omega(\theta)^{-1})\), where the precision \(\Omega(\theta)\) is a parameters7 matrix parameter and the hyperparameters are its free values. This is the correlated prior that quadratic_penalty() cannot express: in a quadratic penalty one scale multiplies a constant matrix, while here the hyperparameters reach every entry of the matrix.

Usage

structured_penalty(structure)

Arguments

structure

A parameters7 matrix_parameter, read as the prior's precision. Pass parameters7::inverse_of(s) to put s on the covariance side instead.

It may be rank deficient, giving an improper prior: is_proper() then returns FALSE and the constant uses the rank and the log pseudo-determinant. A rank-deficient structure can be used only on the precision side, because parameters7::inverse_of() rejects it, a singular matrix having no inverse.

Value

A StructuredPenalty() object whose hyperparameters are the structure's free_names, each unconstrained and on an identity link.

The value

Writing \(\Omega\) for the precision, which is the matrix that the structure supplies,

$$\rho(\beta; \theta) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\beta'\Omega(\theta)\beta - \tfrac{1}{2}\log\mathrm{pdet}\,\Omega(\theta) + \tfrac{r}{2}\log 2\pi,$$

with \(r\) the structure's rank. For a full-rank structure this is the negative log-density of the multivariate normal distribution with mean zero and precision \(\Omega(\theta)\); the examples compare it with a direct evaluation of that density.

The structure is the precision

The matrix that the structure supplies is the prior's precision: \(\Omega = M(\eta)\). This follows from the construction and is not an option, because \(\rho\) is a negative log-density and the matrix that enters its quadratic form is the precision.

The choice of the side on which a structure is placed still matters, because the two readings are different priors. For a positive definite matrix they agree only where \(M = M^{-1}\), that is at the identity. The inverse of an AR(1) matrix is tridiagonal, so for a dimension of three or more it is an AR(1) matrix only at zero correlation. To place a structure s on the covariance side, build the family whose value is its inverse,

structured_penalty(parameters7::inverse_of(s))

which carries \(\partial_k \Sigma^{-1} = -\Sigma^{-1}B_k\Sigma^{-1}\), with \(B_k = \partial_k\Sigma\) the derivative of the covariance, and its higher orders inside the structure, where the log-determinant stays exact. For parameters7::ar1() and parameters7::autoregressive() the inverse has a constructor of its own, parameters7::ar1_inv() and parameters7::autoregressive_inv(), and a structure closed under inversion requires no wrapper.

The derivatives

Every derivative is computed from the derivative arrays that the structure supplies. The hyperparameter gradient is \(\tfrac{1}{2}\beta'A_k\beta - \tfrac{1}{2}\partial_k\log\mathrm{pdet}\,\Omega\), with \(A_k = \partial_k\Omega\) the structure's param_d1; the Hessian uses param_d2, and the mixed block is \(A_k\beta\). No conversion between covariance and precision happens in this package: a structure meant for the covariance side is a different structure, and it supplies its own arrays.

No map

There is no map argument. A linear image of a structured precision is a different precision, and composing it into the structure, where its log-determinant stays exact, is left to parameters7.

See also

quadratic_penalty() for one scale on a fixed matrix, additive_penalty() for a sum of quadratics, distrib_penalty() for a coordinatewise prior, parameters7::log_cholesky() and parameters7::ar1() for structures to pass in, penalty_readable() for the interpretable quantities (a scale, a correlation) of a structure that declares them through parameters7::param_readable().

Examples

# An AR(1) prior on four coefficients: two hyperparameters reach every
# entry of the precision.
pen <- structured_penalty(parameters7::ar1(4))
pen@params
#> [1] "log_scale" "z_rho"    
theta <- list(log_scale = 0.2, z_rho = 0.5)
b <- c(0.3, -0.1, 0.4, 0.2)
penalty_value(pen, b, theta)
#> [1] 3.858268

# The Hessian is the matrix of the structure, read as a precision.
Om <- parameters7::param_value(parameters7::ar1(4),
                               c(0.2, 0.5))
max(abs(penalty_hessian(pen, b, theta) - unclass(Om)))
#> [1] 0

# The same structure read as a covariance is a different prior at the same
# free values: its Hessian is the inverse of that matrix.
cov <- structured_penalty(parameters7::inverse_of(parameters7::ar1(4)))
max(abs(penalty_hessian(cov, b, theta) - solve(unclass(Om))))
#> [1] 5.551115e-17
c(precision = penalty_value(pen, b, theta),
  covariance = penalty_value(cov, b, theta))
#>  precision covariance 
#>   3.858268   3.885654 

# The covariance reading is the negative log-density of the multivariate
# normal with covariance S, written out directly.
S <- unclass(Om)
penalty_value(cov, b, theta) -
  (0.5 * sum(b * solve(S, b)) +
     0.5 * as.numeric(determinant(S, logarithm = TRUE)$modulus) +
     2 * log(2 * pi))
#> [1] 0

# At a zero log-Cholesky free vector the structure is the identity, so the
# penalty equals the plain ridge at lambda = 1, up to rounding.
s <- structured_penalty(parameters7::log_cholesky(3))
z <- as.list(stats::setNames(rep(0, length(s@params)), s@params))
bb <- c(0.4, -1.1, 0.7)
penalty_value(s, bb, z) - penalty_value(ridge_penalty(n_coef = 3), bb,
                                        list(lambda = 1))
#> [1] 0
